title: Transferred model structure on associative algebras
statement:
Use the model-category and universe conventions of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. A combinatorial model category is complete, cocomplete and locally presentable with both weak factorization systems generated by sets, as defined in [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]. Let $\mathcal M$ be such a category, equipped with an associative unital monoidal product $\odot$ with its associativity and unit isomorphisms, not assumed symmetric. Assume both $X\odot-$ and $-\odot X$ have right adjoints for every $X$ (biclosedness), the tensor unit $\mathbf1$ is cofibrant, and the pushout product of two cofibrations is a cofibration, trivial if either factor is trivial. Here the pushout product of $a:A\to B$ and $b:C\to D$ is $(B\odot C)\amalg_{A\odot C}(A\odot D)\to B\odot D$. Assume the following nonsymmetric monoid axiom: the class generated under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts by all finite iterated pushout products $a_1\mathbin\square\cdots\mathbin\square a_n$, where each $a_i$ is either a trivial cofibration or $0\to X_i$ for an arbitrary object $X_i$, and at least one is a trivial cofibration, consists of weak equivalences. Transfinite composition means the composite of an ordinal-indexed sequence continuous at every limit ordinal. A strict associative unital algebra is an object $A$ with maps $A\odot A\to A$ and $\mathbf1\to A$ satisfying the associativity and two unit identities using the monoidal constraints; its morphisms preserve these maps. Write $\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal M)$ for their category and $U$ for the forgetful functor.

There is a combinatorial model structure on $\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal M)$ whose fibrations and weak equivalences are exactly the maps sent by $U$ to fibrations and weak equivalences of $\mathcal M$. The free algebra functor $T$, left adjoint to $U$, and $U$ form a Quillen adjunction, meaning that $T$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations; $T(X)=\coprod_{n\geq0}X^{\odot n}$ with $X^{\odot0}=\mathbf1$, multiplication concatenating the factors and unit the zeroth summand. For any generating cofibrations $I$ and generating trivial cofibrations $J$ of $\mathcal M$, $T(I)$ and $T(J)$ generate the two lifting systems in the algebra category. The functor $U$ sends cofibrant algebras to cofibrant objects of $\mathcal M$.

source.place: Definitions 3.2 and 3.6; Corollaries 3.14 and 3.15. The nonsymmetric monoid axiom is Muro, Homotopy theory of nonsymmetric operads, Definition 9.1 (arbitrary auxiliary objects); the printed cofibrancy restriction in Haugseng Definition 3.11 is not used. See Source error in report.

external.place: Muro Definition 9.1, printed p. 1591; Section 10, pp. 1595-1597 (matrix graphs).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-associative-word-filtration] to the underlying biclosed monoidal category. It supplies the explicit tensor-word monad $P=UT$, its identification of algebras with strict associative unital algebras, the adjunction $T\dashv U$, creation of filtered colimits, and the initial algebra $\mathbf1$. Since $P$ preserves filtered colimits, it preserves $\aleph_0$-filtered colimits. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-monad-presentability] with a singleton set of sorts and base $\mathcal M$: $\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal M)$ is locally presentable and complete and cocomplete. All sets and filtered diagrams here use the fixed universe of the hypotheses.

source.place: Section 3.2, tensor-word construction and Theorem 3.8; accessible-monad presentability input.

proof.text: Fix any generating sets $I,J$ as in the statement. Put $W'=U^{-1}W$ and $F'=U^{-1}F$. Adjunction identifies a square with left side $T(i)$ and right side $p$ with the corresponding square with left side $i$ and right side $U(p)$; the bijection also identifies their diagonal fillers. Consequently $T(I)^{\square}=F'\cap W'$ and $T(J)^{\square}=F'$. Define $C'={}^{\square}(F'\cap W')$ and $D'={}^{\square}F'$. Apply [lem-coef-presentable-small-object-factorization] to each of the small sets $T(I),T(J)$ in the locally presentable algebra category. It gives functorial factorizations into $(C',F'\cap W')$ and $(D',F')$. These pairs are weak factorization systems: for either set $S=T(I)$ or $S=T(J)$, let $R=S^{\square}$ and $L={}^{\square}R$. Every member of $S$ belongs to $L$, so $L^{\square}\subseteq S^{\square}=R$; the defining lifting property of $L$ gives $R\subseteq L^{\square}$. Thus $R=L^{\square}$ as well as $L={}^{\square}R$, and the displayed functorial factorizations supply the remaining axiom.

source.place: Theorem 3.8, small-object factorizations and adjunction on lifting squares.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal K$ be the weakly saturated class of maps specified in the nonsymmetric monoid axiom of the statement, so $\mathcal K\subseteq W$. If $f:X\to Y$ is a trivial cofibration and $T(X)\to A$ is any algebra morphism, the filtration of [lem-coef-associative-word-filtration] presents $U(A)\to U(A\amalg_{T(X)}T(Y))$ as a countable composite of pushouts of $q_n$. Each $q_n$ is an alternating iterated pushout product of copies of $f$ and $0\to U(A)$, with $n\geq1$, so is one of the generators of $\mathcal K$. In particular $U(A)$ is not assumed cofibrant. Thus this underlying pushout map belongs to $\mathcal K$. A small coproduct of trivial cofibrations is a trivial cofibration: against a fibration, choose a filler on each summand and combine them by the coproduct universal property. Because $T$ is a left adjoint, coproducts of maps $T(j)$ are $T(\coprod j)$. Therefore the same conclusion applies to pushouts of small coproducts of maps of $T(J)$.

source.place: Theorem 3.10 and proof of Corollary 3.14; use the arbitrary-object monoid axiom of Muro Definition 9.1, not Haugseng Definition 3.11 as printed.

proof.text: Consider a relative $T(J)$-cell complex, a continuous small ordinal chain of the pushouts in step 3. By creation of filtered colimits in [lem-coef-associative-word-filtration], its underlying chain is continuous at each nonzero limit ordinal. Refine each successor map by its countable filtration from step 3, and concatenate these countable chains in ordinal order. At the inserted and original limit ordinals take the colimits; these give the same objects by the colimit universal property. This exhibits the underlying composite in $\mathcal K$, and hence in $W$. Now take any $d\in D'$ and factor it, using [lem-coef-presentable-cellular-factorization] for $T(J)$, as $p\circ c$ with $c$ a relative $T(J)$-cell map and $p\in T(J)^{\square}=F'$. The left lifting property of $d$ against $p$ makes $d$ an arrow retract of $c$: for $d:X\to Y$ and $c:X\to Z$, lift the square with top $c$, bottom $1_Y$ to obtain $h:Y\to Z$ with $hd=c$ and $ph=1_Y$; the retract squares are $(1_X,h)$ and $(1_X,p)$. Thus $U(d)$ is a retract of the weak equivalence $U(c)$, so $D'\subseteq W'$.

source.place: Theorem 3.8 and Corollary 3.14; cellular acyclicity, refining the filtration instead of asserting arbitrary transfinite closure of W.

proof.text: Since $F'\cap W'\subseteq F'$, left orthogonality gives $D'\subseteq C'$, and step 4 gives $D'\subseteq C'\cap W'$. Conversely let $f\in C'\cap W'$ and use the second functorial factorization of step 2 to write $f=p\circ d$ with $d\in D'$ and $p\in F'$. Step 4 and two-out-of-three for $W'$ give $p\in W'$, so $f$ lifts against $p$. The explicit retract construction of step 4 makes $f$ a retract of $d$. Since the left lifting class $D'$ is retract closed by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], $f\in D'$. Hence $D'=C'\cap W'$. The classes $W'$ inherit retract closure and two-out-of-three from $W$ under the functor $U$. Step 1 gives completeness and cocompleteness, and step 2 now gives exactly the two functorial weak factorization systems required in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. These establish the claimed model structure; local presentability and the generating sets in step 2 make it combinatorial.

source.place: Theorem 3.8, recognition by the two lifting systems; Definition 3.6 and Corollary 3.14.

proof.text: For any cofibration $i$ of $\mathcal M$ and any algebra trivial fibration $p$, the adjoint lifting-square bijection of step 2 turns lifting $T(i)$ against $p$ into lifting $i$ against the trivial fibration $U(p)$. Thus $T(i)\in C'$. If $i$ is a trivial cofibration and $p\in F'$, then $U(p)$ is a fibration; every square from $i$ to $U(p)$ has a filler by the model lifting axiom. The adjunction sends that filler to a filler for the original square from $T(i)$ to $p$, proving $T(i)\in D'=C'\cap W'$. This is precisely the claimed Quillen condition in the model-category convention [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. The explicit formula for $T$, its unit and multiplication are already supplied in step 1 by [lem-coef-associative-word-filtration].

source.place: Definition 3.6 and Corollary 3.14: Quillen property from the adjunction on lifting squares.

proof.text: We next prove that any relative $T(I)$-cell complex starting at the initial algebra has cofibrant underlying objects and cofibration underlying structure maps. The initial underlying object is $\mathbf1$, cofibrant by hypothesis. Suppose the current algebra $A$ has cofibrant underlying object and a successor attaches a small coproduct of $T(i)$, $i\in I$. Write it as a single free attachment $T(f)$, where $f=\coprod i$ is a cofibration (fill against each trivial fibration summand by summand). In [lem-coef-associative-word-filtration], $j:0\to U(A)$ is now a cofibration. The pushout-product hypothesis, iterated over the displayed alternating factors $j,f,\ldots,j,f,j$, makes each $q_n$ a cofibration. Pushouts remain cofibrations by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], and the countable composite remains a cofibration by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting], with the fixed right class the trivial fibrations of $\mathcal M$. Hence the successor object is cofibrant. At any nonzero limit stage, $U$ creates the filtered colimit; apply [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] with right class the trivial fibrations to the continuous chain, including the initial cofibration $0\to\mathbf1$, to conclude that the limit object is cofibrant. This completes transfinite induction, without requiring the domains of the generating maps $I$ to be cofibrant.

source.place: Corollary 3.15; the word-filtration argument for Muro Lemma 9.4, specialized directly to associative algebras.

proof.text: Finally let $A$ be a cofibrant algebra. Apply [lem-coef-presentable-cellular-factorization] to its initial map using $T(I)$, giving $\mathbf1\xrightarrow{c}Z\xrightarrow{p}A$ with $c$ cellular and $p\in T(I)^{\square}=F'\cap W'$. Cofibrancy of $A$ gives a section $s:A\to Z$ of $p$ by lifting its initial map against $p$. Thus $U(A)$ is a retract of $U(Z)$, which is cofibrant by step 7. Retract closure of cofibrations from [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] applied to the initial maps proves that $U(A)$ is cofibrant. This proves the last clause.

source.place: Corollary 3.15 and Muro Lemma 9.4: retract of a free-cell algebra.

lean.statement: theorem associativeAlgebraModelTransfer {M : Type u} [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [MonoidalCategory M] (_hM : CombinatorialModelCategory.{u, v, v} M) (_leftAdj : ∀ X : M, ((tensoringLeft M).obj X).IsLeftAdjoint) (_rightAdj : ∀ X : M, ((tensoringRight M).obj X).IsLeftAdjoint) (_unit : IsCofibrant (𝟙_ M)) (_pushoutProduct : ∀ (f g : Arrow M), Cofibration f.hom → Cofibration g.hom → Cofibration ((MonoidalCategory.Arrow.pushoutProduct.obj f).obj g).hom ∧ (WeakEquivalence f.hom ∨ WeakEquivalence g.hom → WeakEquivalence ((MonoidalCategory.Arrow.pushoutProduct.obj f).obj g).hom)) (_monoidAxiom : NonsymmetricMonoidAxiom M) : ∃ W : AssociativeWordFiltration.Construction M, Nonempty (AssociativeAlgebraTransfer W)
